name: Hog Island Type A, Design 1022 — interwar unarmed merchant exterior
representation: Historical Design 1022 proportions provide a representative prewar merchant appearance. This is not a nation-specific merchant identity or a claim that every convoy consists of Hog Islanders. Gameplay tonnage, hull counts, carrying capacity, crew and economic rules remain unchanged.
axes: right-handed: X bow-positive; Y up; Z transverse; loaded waterline Y=0
geometrySource: Original reconstruction of the Design 1022 three-island general arrangement and 1920 U.S. Shipping Board particulars. A distinct hull, island layout, bridge, funnel, hatch stations, mast rig and boats; not a rescaled Liberty, voxel conversion or downloaded mesh.
accuracy: Original unarmed merchant exterior suitable as a representative interwar freighter, not an exact reconstruction of every ship or national fleet. Principal dimensions and deck arrangement follow the cited original plans. Hull station breadths and underwater end shapes are approximations measured from plan views/profile; no complete offsets table was available. Small fittings, propeller pitch, plate weathering, lifeboat interiors and lowered sea-going boom pose are inferred. No naval conversion armament, modern antennas or gun tubs. Mesh dimensions and representative appearance do not change gameplay GRT, crew, speed, cargo or armament. Exterior only. Requires native visual review before adoption.
license: Original WNT1922 geometry and paint albedo remain under project LICENSE.md; no public reuse license is granted. Independently licensed Poly Haven maps remain CC0-1.0. Historical reference rasters are not embedded or redistributed in the mesh.

sources.title: U.S. Shipping Board, Register of Ships Owned, August 1, 1920 — particulars No. 32, S.S. Quistconck
sources.usedFor: Original government particulars: 401 ft overall, 54 ft molded beam, 32 ft depth, loaded draft 24 ft 5 3/16 in; inspected full scan. The historical GRT entry is reference only, not assigned to the game.

sources.title: Design 1022 general arrangement, sheet 1 — original profile and midship section reproduced by ShipScribe
sources.usedFor: Distinct three-island hull, sheer/counter stern, bridge versus engine house placement, two cargo masts and central derrick posts. Underwater offsets are inferred, not certified.

sources.title: Design 1022 general arrangement, sheet 2 — original deck plans reproduced by ShipScribe
sources.usedFor: Hatch sizes and locations; separate navigating and flying bridge; boat deck with four 24 ft lifeboats; forecastle, poop, engine skylights, cargo winches and deck fittings.
